{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention training (based on the 4C/ID model and focused on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention) would improve response times in shoot scenarios compared to an active control group.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based intervention training focused on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control training resembling traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Response time (in milliseconds) between the detection of a black handgun in a video scenario and the participant's initial motor response (shot taken).",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers recruited from a university campus, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary; debriefing provided at the end.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with the within-subject factor Time and the between-subject factor Group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered (www.aspredicted.org #119896)",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants used a gas-operated replica of a Heckler and Koch SFP9 handgun. The intervention training was based on the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID). Exclusions were applied for participants who did not shoot in at least one of the shoot scenarios."
}
